fields.statement: At b411878: go test ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/rex-install passes; the script now greps rhiza.lua for the launch key entering the mode (client.mode.enter, name = MODE), default keys for roadmap and model, settings keys = {}, and rex.bind(MODE .. "/" .. k, "rhiza_app_" .. app). Unit tests TestRexInstallBindsAKeyPerAppInTheKeyMode (one unique key per launcher app, each written in DEFAULT_KEYS), TestRexDefaultKeysAreMnemonicAndUnique and TestRexInstallKeepsKeyOverridesOnReinstall pass. A scratch rex install wrote 16 DEFAULT_KEYS entries (accept=a, change-show=c, ... why=w), all distinct, one for each of the 16 rhiza_app_* actions, in an exclusive mode "rhiza" with escape bound to exit. That matches decision rex-app-keys-default-overridable (default mnemonic keys, remapped through settings.keys, which a reinstall keeps) and native-rex-prefix-configurable (launch_key setting, default ctrl+a a). Rex docs confirm rex.mode exclusive and client.mode.enter { name, once }. gofmt, go vet and go test ./... pass. make check's only failure is the stale .rhiza/rendered from model writes, which this commit doesn't touch. Note: a settings.keys remap onto another app's default key (e.g. the comment's own example roadmap = "m" collides with model) binds both, and the winner depends on pairs order.
